chapter_theme: The opening of Pambatti Siddhar's song, a snake-charmer's kummi whose every stanza ends by telling the snake to dance (ஆடு பாம்பே). The first nine stanzas worship the Lord as the fullness in all lives, the void that cannot be pointed at, and the flood of bliss that becomes the worlds it made; the next ten praise the true guru who takes the disciple's body, goods and life, shows the Real like a fruit in the palm, corrects false gurus, and has powers such as leaving one body for another and circling the sky with a pill. Then the serpent itself is praised, ornament of Siva, Vishnu and Parvati, and the Siddhar begins to boast of his power over the eight nagas.
structure_note: Four sections by the printed headings: கடவுள் வணக்கம் (1980 to 1988), குரு வணக்கம் (1989 to 1998), பாம்பினது சிறப்பு (1999 to 2003) and the start of சித்தர் வல்லபங் கூறல் (2004, continued in chapter 103). The refrain shifts from ஆடு பாம்பே to the imperative ஆடாய் பாம்பே at 1989. The snake addressed is on a plain reading the charmer's cobra and on the traditional reading the mind or the coiled power in the body; the readings below give the stanza's own content, not the refrain.

1980.reading: The opening stanza is almost all refrain: be clear, be clear, snake, having seen Siva's fine feet, and dance saying that we have seen the Lord's feet.
1980.nuance: தெளிந்து (becoming clear) is repeated five times; the song's first instruction is clarity, and its first claim is the sight of the feet. Tradition takes the snake as the mind or the kundalini; the stanza itself only addresses a dancing snake.

1981.reading: Thinking on the First One's feet even while toiling, and saying that the lasting state is for ever our own, eternal, and the great release, praise him again and again and dance.
1981.nuance: நீடுபதம் (the lasting state) and பெரிய முத்தி are claimed as நமக்கு சொந்தம், our own property, a confidence that marks the whole song.

1982.reading: Bow to the feet of the Giver who is everywhere as fullness like the light in gold, who abides with beauty like scent in a flower, and who dwells fitted within the many living beings, and dance.
1982.nuance: The three similes make pervasion inseparable rather than spatial: light is not apart from the gold nor scent from the flower. பூரணம் is the Siddhars' name for God as the whole.

1983.reading: Thinking again and again of the fragrant flower-feet of the Lord who fills every life as oil fills the sesame seed, so that love and devotion rise as they truly are, shrink, be contained, be clear and dance.
1983.nuance: எள்ளில் எண்ணெய் is a stock Siddhar image for a presence that pervades without being visible (Sivavakkiyar uses it for the Vedanta). ஒடுங்கி அடங்கி, shrink and be contained, is addressed to the snake and reads naturally as a yogic withdrawal of the senses.

1984.reading: Think without ceasing on our First God who gave the cosmos and the body, bow with love, praise him so that the eight directions resound, and seek him with a single mind, and dance.
1984.nuance: அண்டபிண்டம் தந்த names the Lord as giver of both macrocosm and body in one word. ஏகமனம், a single mind, is the stanza's practice.

1985.reading: Worship the pure Substance made of light, weep and cry out தொந்தோந்தோம், stand firm on the path that does not swerve from right, think and think and melt, and dance.
1985.nuance: வஸ்து (the Substance, the Real) is the song's favoured name for God, used again in 1986 and 1993. தொந்தோந்தோ(ம்) is read here as a cry of joy or a drum sound, like the Naladiyar's டொண்; a reading that hears தொந்தத்தசி (that thou art) in it is possible but not secure.

1986.reading: Praise the dense Substance that is formless and formed, that is the twilight and the end, the light and the Agama, the Lady and the guru and the living soul, and dance.
1986.nuance: அருவாயும் உருவாயும் is the Saiva pair of formless and formed. அந்தி may be twilight (the junction, as the yogis' time) or a corruption of அந்தம் doubled with the next word. திரு here could be Lakshmi, Shakti or simply the holy; the stanza's point is that one Substance is all these.

1987.reading: Knowing by subtle intellect the void and emptiness that cannot be pointed at or shown, so that fault is gone, and saying that we have reached and caught it, spread your hood in bliss and dance.
1987.nuance: சுட்டிக்காட்டி ஒண்ணாத, what cannot be pointed at, is the stanza's definition of the void, and பாழ் and சூனியம் are set side by side as its names. சூட்சமதி, subtle intellect, is the faculty that knows it. The claim to have caught (எட்டிப் பிடித்தோம்) the uncatchable is the Siddhar's deliberate paradox.

1988.reading: See the flood of bliss that gave birth to every life and every world, stood outside them and enjoyed its holy play, and afterwards stood as those very lives and worlds, and dance.
1988.nuance: The stanza holds transcendence and immanence in sequence: first புறம்பாய் (outside), then ஆகியும் நின்ற (standing as them). திருவிளையாட்டு, holy play, is creation as the Lord's sport.

1989.reading: Praise our true guru who stood and received as gift the body, the goods and the life that were declared his, so that mind, speech and body all three are in accord, and dance.
1989.nuance: உடல் பொருள் ஆவி, body, wealth and life, is the formula of total surrender to the guru; தத்தம் ஆக ... தானம் வாங்கி says the guru accepted them as a gift. மனம் வாக்கு காயம், the three instruments, must agree in the praise.

1990.reading: Praise the feet of the true guru who talks sense to the false gurus who preach false religions and sends them off on the good path, and who declares which religion is true and makes one join it, and dance.
1990.nuance: பொய்ம்மதம் and மெய்ம்மதம், false and true religion, frame the stanza; the true guru is defined by his effect on false gurus, correcting rather than destroying them.

1991.reading: Dance having seen the feet of the full true guru who, having seen the true Thing that is beyond the Vedas, sets his mind on it and declares what the meaning of the Veda is, and teaches what the meaning of knowledge is.
1991.nuance: The guru knows the Veda's meaning because he has seen what lies beyond it (வேதம் கடந்த மெய்ப்பொருள்); the ordering is deliberate, experience first and scripture explained from it.

1992.reading: Having thrown off the thieving mind, find with love the true guru who is able to show the Thing that is as it is, truly, like a fruit in the palm of the hand, and smile and rejoice and dance.
1992.nuance: உள்ளங்கையில் கனி போல, like a fruit in the palm, is the stanza's measure of the guru's teaching: direct and graspable. கள்ள மனம், the thieving or deceitful mind, is what must be set aside first.

1993.reading: Bow constantly without doubt to the guru who is our life and who makes the First Substance known like a mirror in the palm, and raise your golden hood and dance.
1993.nuance: The mirror in the palm pairs with the fruit in the palm of 1992: the guru does not describe the Real, he reflects it. எங்கள் உயிரான குரு makes the guru the disciple's very life. தமனியப் படம், the golden hood, is the one place the snake's body enters the praise.

1994.reading: Worship the feet of the pure guru who saw the body's state perish, then took the state of firmness within and found the pure state that lives for all time, and dance.
1994.nuance: கற்புநிலை is read as a state of steadfastness (கற்பு as firmness, not wifely chastity); a reading that hears கற்பம், the rejuvenating kalpa of the medical Siddhars, in it would make the guru one who outlives the body by medicine. எக்காலமும் வாழும் is the Siddhar claim of deathlessness.

1995.reading: Who can tell the power of the guru whose practice is to leave one body and leap into another? Bow to the true guru who shows the way to win release more and more, and dance.
1995.nuance: கூடுவிட்டுக் கூடுபாய்தல், leaving the cage for a cage, is the Tamil phrase for entering another body, one of the eight siddhis; the stanza joins that power to showing the way to release, so the siddhi is not set against liberation.

1996.reading: Say that your refuge is the flower-feet of the able guru who, with a pill that contains the eight directions and the open space of the cosmos, goes round swiftly in a circle, and dance.
1996.nuance: குளிகை is the pill of the alchemists and sorcerers, traditionally a mercury pill held in the mouth that lets the siddha fly or vanish; the stanza has the guru circle the sky with it. அடக்கிய may mean the pill holds the directions within it or that the guru has subdued them. Read as a claim of power, not a method.

1997.reading: Praise as refuge the golden feet of the causal guru who lives without his vessel perishing, alongside the First Maker who is beyond the kalpa-ages, and dance with a mind full.
1997.nuance: கடம் (the pot, the body) that does not perish continues 1994's claim that the guru's body outlasts time; காரணக்குரு, the causal guru, sets him beside the ஆதி கர்த்தா as cause rather than creature.

1998.reading: Even if a flaw can come to the diamond, no defect will come to the strong body of our Veda-guru who has a vessel to be admired; praise his soft feet and dance.
1998.nuance: The body harder than diamond is the Siddhar ideal of the perfected body (வல்லுடம்பு). வேதகுரு may mean the guru who knows the Veda or, hearing வேதை, the alchemist guru who has transmuted his body; the stanza does not decide.

1999.reading: Naga snake who sits on the Lord's crown, good snake who keeps the poison-sac, hooded snake who makes your home in the underworld, sing and sing and play, and dance.
1999.nuance: The section on the snake's glory begins with three of its homes: Siva's head, its own venom and the nether world (பாதலம்). The poison is called நல்ல, good, kept and not used.

2000.reading: Snake that draws in its head as it enters the hole, coloured snake that coils its body in a circle, true snake that stands without fearing bonds, lift your head and play, and dance.
2000.nuance: The three traits, withdrawing the head to enter the hole, coiling in a mandala and standing unafraid of fetters, are plain snake lore and also the traditional marks of the yogic breath or power entering the channel and coiling at the base; சத்தியப் பாம்பே (true snake) leans the stanza toward the coded sense.

2001.reading: You became the earring of the faultless Siva, the umbrella of the praised Vishnu, and the bracelet of thick-haired Parvati; rejoice at heart without hiding, and dance.
2001.nuance: Three gods, three ornaments: the snake is honoured by the whole pantheon, which gives the charmer's animal its dignity. Vishnu's umbrella is the hood of Adishesha.

2002.reading: You took the great strength that holds up the earth, you became the coloured mat for Vishnu's bed, you gained a sight that makes the armies that see you tremble, and you took the eye for an ear; dance.
2002.nuance: கண்ணே செவியாகக் கொண்டாய் records the belief that snakes hear through their eyes, hence their Sanskrit name chakshushravas; the stanza is natural history and myth together.

2003.reading: You leapt and touched the moon and the sun, you became an ornament for Shankara, you were brought under control by mantra and you coiled in a circle; bend and bend and dance.
2003.nuance: Touching the moon and sun is Rahu the eclipse-serpent on the plain reading; in the Siddhars' cipher sun and moon are the right and left breaths or the fire at the base and the nectar at the crown, so the line can also say the coiled power reaches both. மந்திரத்திற்கு அடங்கினாய் keeps the charmer's craft in view.

2004.reading: We will take the eight nagas in our hands and make them dance, we will show Indra's world right here, we will bind and release the snake that no binding holds; spit out your fierce poison and dance.
2004.nuance: The Siddhar's boast begins. The eight nagas (Ananta, Vasuki, Takshaka, Karkotaka, Padma, Mahapadma, Shankhapala, Kulika) are named in 2014 and 2015; the uncontrollable snake made to spit its poison is on the coded reading the mind or the kundalini emptied of its venom. The stanza presents a power, not a procedure.

links.note: Both poets use oil in the sesame seed for an unseen presence that fills the whole: Pattiragiriyar for the end of the Veda embracing all that moves and stands, Pambatti for the Lord filling every life. Pattiragiriyar asks when he will know it; Pambatti tells the snake to think on it until devotion rises.

Tirumular tells the disciple to give the guru the goods he has, his body and his life; Pambatti's guru has already received body, goods and life (உடல் பொருள் ஆவி) as a gift. The formula of surrender is the same, and both make it the mark of the true guru relation.

Both define the false guru: Tirumular as the fool without inner feeling who never sees the Veda-Agama path and reviles others, Pambatti as the preacher of false religions. Tirumular only condemns; Pambatti's true guru talks sense to the false ones and sends them onto the good path, a gentler ending to the same diagnosis.

Tirumular lists the body entering another body among the eight siddhis; Pambatti credits the same power, leaving one cage for another, to the guru and asks who can tell its measure. Both treat it as a siddha's attainment, and Pambatti adds that the same guru shows the way to release.

Tirumular's yogi in the eighth year shows no grey hair or wrinkles; Pambatti's guru has a strong body that no defect can touch, harder than diamond. Both hold that practice perfects the body itself, not only the mind.

The boast of making the eight nagas dance in the hand is carried out in the dialogue of 2014 to 2018, where the eight are named, set in the eight directions of a chakra with letters and mantra, and the Siddhars are told to take the hooded ones in hand so they spit their poison.

source_issues: 1985 line 2 தொழுதழு தலற்றிற் தொந்தோந்தோ மெனவே: தலற்றிற் is unmetrical and probably a slip for அலற்றி; தொந்தோந்தோம் is left unexplained by the text.
1986 line 1 அந்தியாயும் may be a corruption of a word paired with அந்தமாயும் in the next line.
The refrain changes form from ஆடு பாம்பே (1980 to 1988) to ஆடாய் பாம்பே (1989 to 1998) and back to ஆடு பாம்பே (1999 to 2004); the section headings are the editor's.
